section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Defense Mechanisms (Complete Set)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who was badly bullied in Class 3 has no conscious memory of the incident at all years later, though it still subtly affects his behaviour. This unconscious blocking of a distressing memory from awareness is:
explanation: Repression is the unconscious exclusion of painful memories/impulses from conscious awareness — distinct from denial, a conscious-level refusal of a still-remembered fact.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Defense Mechanisms (Complete Set)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher who was scolded by the principal comes home and snaps angrily at her own children over a trivial matter, even though they did nothing wrong. Redirecting an emotion from its true source to a safer target is:
explanation: Displacement redirects an emotional response toward a substitute target that is safer to express it toward than the original source.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Defense Mechanisms (Complete Set)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student with strong aggressive impulses channels this energy into becoming a highly disciplined, competitive boxer instead of getting into fights. Redirecting an unacceptable impulse into a socially acceptable, constructive activity is:
explanation: Sublimation channels an unacceptable impulse into a socially valued, constructive outlet — considered the most 'mature' defense mechanism.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch11 — Defense Mechanisms (Complete Set)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A child who secretly feels intense jealousy toward a new sibling instead behaves with exaggerated, almost excessive affection and care toward the baby. Expressing the opposite of one's true, unacceptable feeling is:
explanation: Reaction formation converts an unacceptable impulse into its opposite at the conscious/behavioural level.
